title: Coordinatewise graph model structure
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathbf V=\operatorname{Ch}(R)$ carry the projective combinatorial model structure of [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. For every small set $S$, the graph category $\mathbf G_S=\prod_{(s,t)\in S^2}\mathbf V$ has the product model structure: weak equivalences, fibrations, and cofibrations are exactly the maps that have the corresponding class in every coordinate. It is complete, cocomplete, combinatorial, locally presentable, left proper, and tractable. Generating cofibrations and generating trivial cofibrations are obtained by placing one generating map of $\mathbf V$ in one coordinate and the initial map in all other coordinates; these sets have cofibrant sources.

source.place: Muro Remark 10.2, p. 1596 (PDF page 56), with Remark 2.3 for single-coordinate generating maps. Completeness, cocompleteness, left properness and tractability follow coordinatewise from the projective chain model; local presentability also follows from the existing ordinary-presheaf presentability theorem for the discrete category on S squared.

proof.text: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ containing $R$ and the small set $S$, and work with complexes having $\mathcal U$-small underlying modules. Put $T=S\times S$. The projective model supplied by [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] is combinatorial, with the conventions in [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]: in particular $\mathbf V$ has small Hom sets, all small limits and colimits, is locally presentable, and has two functorial weak factorization systems. Use its quasi-isomorphisms $W$, cofibrations $C$, and degreewise-surjective fibrations $F$ throughout; no monoidal localization assertion is needed.

source.place: Remark 10.2: input model; agent unpacking of the two cited model-structure statements.

proof.text: A morphism of graphs $X\to Y$ is a family $(f_t:X_t\to Y_t)_{t\in T}$, with identities and composition taken in each coordinate. For a small diagram $D$, form $(\lim D)_t=\lim D_t$ and $(\operatorname{colim}D)_t=\operatorname{colim}D_t$ in $\mathbf V$. A graph cone (respectively cocone) is precisely a family of coordinate cones (respectively cocones); their unique universal maps assemble to the unique graph map. These formulas prove completeness and cocompleteness, including the empty limits and colimits. Since $T$ is small, the product of the coordinate Hom sets is still $\mathcal U$-small.

source.place: Remark 10.2; agent coordinate universal-property calculation from Step 1.

proof.text: Let $D_T$ be the discrete category on $T$: its only arrows are identities. A functor $D_T^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf V$ is exactly a family of objects indexed by $T$, and a natural transformation is exactly a family of maps, since its identity naturality equations impose no condition. Sending a family to this functor and evaluating back are inverse on objects and maps. Thus the graph category is the presheaf category $\operatorname{Fun}(D_T^{\mathrm{op}},\mathbf V)$ under this identification. Apply [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability]: $D_T$ is $\mathcal U$-small, $\mathbf V$ is locally presentable by Step 1, and its pullbacks exist by Step 1. The resulting local presentability is relative to the same $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Lines 90-96; agent identification with presheaves on the discrete category.

proof.text: Define $W_T,C_T,F_T$ to mean membership in $W,C,F$ at every coordinate. Two-out-of-three for $W_T$ and retract closure of all three classes follow by evaluating each equation or retract diagram at $t$ and applying the corresponding model axiom of Step 1. In a graph lifting square, each coordinate is a lifting square in $\mathbf V$. If its left map is in $C_T$ and its right map is in $F_T\cap W_T$, choose the coordinate fillers; their family fills the graph square. The same argument applies to $C_T\cap W_T$ against $F_T$. There are no extra naturality conditions between distinct coordinates.

source.place: Remarks 10.2 and 2.3; agent verification of weak equivalences, retracts, and lifting axioms.

proof.text: Apply each of the two functorial factorizations of Step 1 to every $f_t$, and use the resulting family of middle objects and maps to factor $f$. This gives $C_T$ followed by $F_T\cap W_T$, and $C_T\cap W_T$ followed by $F_T$. On a square between graph maps, take the componentwise middle-object map; the two factorization equations and the identity and composition laws hold because they do at every $t$. These are functorial graph factorizations. To check that the classes are mutually characterized by lifting, factor any map having the proposed left lifting property and lift against its right factor: write $f=pc$ and the lift $h$ satisfies $hf=c$, $ph=1$. The pairs $(1,h)$ and $(1,p)$ exhibit $f$ as an arrow-category retract of $c$. Retract closure from Step 4 puts it in the proposed left class. Dually, if $f$ has the proposed right lifting property, factor $f=pc$ and lift against $c$ to obtain $h$ with $hc=1$ and $fh=p$; the pairs $(c,1)$ and $(h,1)$ exhibit $f$ as a retract of $p$. Together with Steps 2 and 4 this proves the product model axioms.

source.place: Remarks 10.2 and 2.3; agent factorization and retract argument using the model axioms in Step 1.

proof.text: Take the generating sets $I=\{S^{n+1}\hookrightarrow D^n:n\in\mathbf Z\}$ and $J=\{0\to D^n:n\in\mathbf Z\}$ from [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. For $t\in T$, define $L_t(A)$ to have coordinate $A$ at $t$ and $0$ elsewhere, and define $L_t(u)$ to have coordinate $u$ at $t$ and $1_0:0\to0$ elsewhere. A map $L_t(A)\to X$ consists of its arbitrary $t$-component $A\to X_t$ and the unique maps from $0$ in every other coordinate. This gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(L_t(A),X)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,X_t)$ compatible with precomposition and postcomposition. Put $I_T=\{L_t(i):t\in T,i\in I\}$ and $J_T=\{L_t(j):t\in T,j\in J\}$. These are small sets; the off-coordinate initial map is precisely $1_0$, not a map with a nonzero target.

source.place: Remark 2.3, single-coordinate left adjoints, applied to T=S squared; standard chain generators from the cited node.

proof.text: The bijection in Step 6 identifies a square with left side $L_t(i)$ and right side $p$ with a square having left side $i$ and right side $p_t$, and identifies their fillers. Since $I$ and $J$ generate the two lifting systems in $\mathbf V$ by [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], it follows that $I_T^{\pitchfork}=F_T\cap W_T$ and $J_T^{\pitchfork}=F_T$. Step 5 therefore identifies ${}^{\pitchfork}(I_T^{\pitchfork})=C_T$ and ${}^{\pitchfork}(J_T^{\pitchfork})=C_T\cap W_T$. This proves that the proposed sets generate the lifting classes; the next two steps verify smallness and cellular generation as well.

source.place: Remark 2.3; agent lifting-square calculation, not an appeal to a separate product-model theorem.

proof.text: Let $K$ index all domains of maps in $I_T$ and $J_T$, retaining repetitions, so $K$ is small. In the locally presentable graph category of Step 3, [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] gives, for each such domain $A_k$, an infinite regular $\tau_k\in\mathcal U$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(A_k,-)$ preserves all small $\tau_k$-filtered colimits. Let $X_k$ be the set of ordinals below the initial ordinal of cardinality $\tau_k$. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to $(X_k)_{k\in K}$ to get an infinite regular $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ with $|\coprod_kX_k|<\lambda$. The injection $x\mapsto(k,x)$ shows $\tau_k\leq|\coprod_kX_k|<\lambda$ for every $k$. This also applies to the empty family.

The ordinal category $\lambda$ is $\tau_k$-filtered for each $k$: the images of the objects of a diagram with fewer than $\tau_k$ morphisms are fewer than $\lambda$ ordinals below $\lambda$, and their supremum is below $\lambda$ by regularity. That supremum is an upper bound and supplies the cocone; for the empty diagram use $0$. Hence Step 8 gives preservation by $\operatorname{Hom}(A_k,-)$ of every $\lambda$-indexed colimit, in particular of the cellular chains required by [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization]. Apply that node once to $I_T$ and once to $J_T$. Step 2 supplies all small colimits and small Hom sets, Step 6 supplies small generating sets, and Step 8 supplies the small regular cardinal. It gives functorial cellular factorizations and identifies the left lifting classes as retracts of the respective cell maps. With Step 7 these are exactly the two weak factorization systems of Step 5. Thus the model is cofibrantly generated; with Step 3 it is combinatorial in the convention of Step 1.

For the generators in [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], the spheres $S^m$ are dg-projective: their terms are free or zero, and their Hom complex into an acyclic complex is that complex reindexed, with the shift sign, hence is acyclic. Its cofibration criterion makes $0\to S^m$ a cofibration. The composite $0\to S^{n+1}\hookrightarrow D^n$ is also a cofibration: two successive left-lifting fillers give a filler for their composite. Also $0$ is cofibrant since $1_0$ lifts against every map. Thus the sources and targets of both $I$ and $J$ are cofibrant. The map $0\to L_t(A)$ has component $0\to A$ at $t$ and $1_0$ elsewhere, so Step 4 makes $L_t(A)$ cofibrant whenever $A$ is. Consequently $I_T$ and $J_T$ have cofibrant sources and targets. In particular the generating-cofibration condition for tractability in [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] holds, as does the stronger convention requiring cofibrant sources for both generating sets.

source.place: Remark 2.3; agent check of the explicit projective generators and cofibrant sources; tractability convention from the cited chain-model node.

proof.text: For a pushout of $f:A\to A'$ along $i:A\to B$ in the graph category, Step 2 identifies its $t$-component with $B_t\amalg_{A_t}A'_t$. If $f\in W_T$ and $i\in C_T$, [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] applies to this coordinate pushout over the given commutative ring $R$ and makes $B_t\to B_t\amalg_{A_t}A'_t$ a weak equivalence. This holds for every $t$, so the graph pushout map is in $W_T$. The product model is therefore left proper. Local presentability (Step 3), generation (Steps 7-9), and the cofibrant generators (Step 10) give tractability. If $S$ is empty the category has one object and one map, both generating sets are empty, and every assertion is vacuous or a terminal-category universal property. For singleton $S$ every construction reduces to the original chain model.

source.place: Remark 10.2, agent left-properness pushout calculation and tractability check; the source states right properness, whereas left properness here uses the cited chain-model input.
